title: Contact - City of Crowley
key_finding: The City's official contact page lists a Crowley Police Department inside city government, gives departmental phone numbers, names Troy Hebert as Chief of Police, and routes police records requests through the city contact structure.

title: Crowley Police Department
key_finding: Crowley Police Department maintains a live official site with department branding, a current street address, non-emergency contact number, and records-request and contact-request forms.

title: Enforcement
key_finding: The sheriff describes patrol services as dedicated to the citizens of Acadia Parish and says the APSO 911 center dispatches five law-enforcement agencies around the parish, which supports coexistence with municipal agencies rather than a single parishwide replacement of Crowley Police.

title: Methods of Submitting Data
publisher: Louisiana Commission on Law Enforcement and Louisiana Sheriffs' Association
key_finding: Louisiana's official reporting overview says the FBI stopped accepting summary reports through UCR Online as of January 1, 2021 and explains that agencies submit either summary LUCR/SRS data or LIBRS data converted to NIBRS.

title: 2020 Crime in Louisiana
publisher: Louisiana Commission on Law Enforcement and Louisiana Sheriffs' Association
key_finding: The 2020 participating-agency list shows Acadia Parish Sheriff and Crowley Police Department as separate Acadia agencies, while Iota Police Department is marked with an asterisk for reporting under the parish sheriff.

title: Uniform Crime Reporting
key_finding: The legislative audit appendix marks Crowley Police Department 'No' for reporting 2022 data to the FBI, while other Acadia municipalities such as Estherwood, Iota, and Morse are explicitly labeled as reporting through Acadia Parish Sheriff's Office.

title: Crime in Louisiana 2023
publisher: Louisiana Commission on Law Enforcement and Louisiana Sheriffs' Association
key_finding: The certified 2023 Louisiana LIBRS report lists Church Point and Rayne among Acadia-area city agencies and shows Acadia in the metropolitan-county table, but Crowley is absent from the city participation and offense tables, confirming a city-specific public-reporting gap rather than a clean parish replacement.
